dividerScopeDecision.chosen: ONLY the most recent visit gets a divider. The 09 Jan 2026 and 22 Sep 2025 visits render as ordinary Note rows.
dividerScopeDecision.why: Three reasons. First, the chart is answering one question — when did I last see this patient and what has happened since — and one question takes one answer; three bands in an eleven-row ledger is a band every three rows, which turns the device back into the row separator it is trying to stop being. Second, the elapsed statement is only true of the most recent visit; "since the visit on 09 Jan 2026 — 7 events" is a different and less useful claim, and two such counts in one column compete. Third, chunking the whole ledger by visit is a different information architecture, not a divider treatment, and it is not what was asked for.

betterConstructionNoted.observation: The proposed wording states a date and a volume but not an elapsed duration. "Since the last visit on 21 Jul 2026" makes the reader compute six weeks from the date. The brief asked the band to "state elapsed time and volume", and as written it states a date and volume.
betterConstructionNoted.alternative: Putting the duration first delivers the elapsed part directly and keeps the date available: "6 weeks since the last visit — 21 Jul 2026 · 4 events". It also front-loads the number that changes, which is the one worth scanning for.
betterConstructionNoted.secondOrderNote: Reading top-down the reader meets the four events before the band that labels them. The band both closes the group above and introduces the visit below, which is coherent, but a duration-first phrasing would survive that order better because the duration reads as a heading rather than as a caption for what came before.

theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened._status: CONFIRMED ON THE CANVAS. Reported, not fixed, as instructed.
theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened.finding: Yes — the band reads heavier here than the same three cards read on the busy patient.
theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened.mechanism: Two things changed at once. On State 1 the cards competed with a dense ledger of yellow chips and seven teal actions, so they were one voice among several. Here the ledger is deliberately quiet — grey chips, five actions, six empty action cells — so the three cards are the busiest thing on the screen and hold the top third of the page uncontested. A chart whose whole message is "nothing is wrong" opens with three statements of things not done.
theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened.secondMechanism: Equal weight flattens unequal things. A colorectal screening overdue at 58 and an atorvastatin refill the patient may have stopped on purpose are rendered identically. On the busy patient the cards were all genuinely urgent, so uniform weight cost nothing; on this patient it manufactures urgency for at least one of the three.
theFailureModeWasPredictedAndItHappened.whatThisArguesFor: Not a fix in this frame. It argues that the insight band needs either a density rule tied to how much is actually outstanding, or a weight axis on the card so a routine obligation can render lighter than a clinical one. Both are decisions, not corrections.

incidentalFindings.collectPaymentAtZeroBalance: The action row still offers "Collect Payment" while the header reads Balance $0.00. incidentalFindings.allergyIconIsTheLoudestThingOnScreen: The red AttentionFilled glyph on "Moderate: penicillin" is the highest-contrast element on a screen whose entire point is that nothing is wrong. An allergy banner is a standing safety fact and should persist, so this is probably correct — but it is worth knowing that severity chrome does not scale down with severity, and on a quiet patient it dominates.

npveRebuild_agentRules_2026-09-04.sectionText:
## Rules for any agent working in these files

Any agent — Claude, Codex, or other — editing the Figma files or this repo follows the same loop. Work that skips it gets audited and may be superseded.

1. Read before touching: this file, then design-system-schema.json for current state. The schema is the record; chat history and your own memory are not.
2. Audit before building: when the current state is uncertain, run a read-only inventory first and report it. Never build onto an unverified state.
3. One batch at a time, with a stop condition stated up front. A batch that grows past its stop condition becomes two batches.
4. Additive only. Nothing is deleted, and nothing is moved, renamed, or superseded without a record saying so. Archives get a README.
5. No invention. If the library and code lack a pattern, mark it (GAP/DEFECT per the convention) and build with what exists. Recreating a source drawing by hand and calling it a component is a false record, which is worse than the gap.
6. Verify in pixels. Screenshot what you built and look at it. Property readbacks are claims; renders are evidence. After editing a component, re-screenshot its live instances and diff.
7. Record every batch: a dated schema record via an apply-*.js script, backup first, findings to flags[]. A batch without a record did not happen and will be treated as suspect.
8. Report per rule 13: full report to disk, short reply, no tables in chat. Change logs in the file are written in plain graphic-design language, not system jargon.
9. When sources disagree or a decision is needed, stop and report. Precedence (code > Storybook render > library > source) resolves facts, not design decisions.

step8_claudeMd.subsection: ### Sheet and comparison techniques, inserted after rule 15 under Standing rules (CRLF preserved)
text: Adopted 2026-09-05 from the external sidesheet batches (record npveRebuild_extReviewRepairs_2026-09-05).

Sheets are as tall as their content. The Sidesheet master stays 550 by 600. A placed sheet grows or shrinks to fit its body, and the footer sits right under the last row. Never pad a short sheet to 600 or pin its footer to the bottom.

Helpers under a short sheet are transparent. When a rebuilt sheet is shorter than the comparison slot, the Rebuild sub-component carries no fill, so only the sheet shows white. Nothing false extends below it.

Tall content overflows the slot; the slot does not shrink it. When a reference or a rebuilt sheet is taller than the 600 slot, keep it at 1:1 and switch clipping off on that column of the placed comparison instance. Never scale a reference to fit.
New bodies join the shell through its Body content list. Append the new body component to the Sidesheet's Body content preferred values and leave the default alone. Do not fork the shell.
A new state is a new variant of the body it belongs to. Add State=Empty to the existing body set rather than creating a second set or a loose frame.

Values the library lacks may live in a local NPVE collection. Name the collection NPVE/<kind>, record the operator's decision in the schema, claim no code syntax, and add the value to the library to-do list. Never write it into the library from a consuming file.

step5_backupPolicy.status: SURFACED, NOT DECIDED — standing rule 7 (backup before every batch) stands; this batch took its full backup the old way.
step5_backupPolicy.question: Replace the per-batch full-schema backup (design-system-schema.backup-<date>-pre-<batch>.json, 1.4 MB each, 89 files today) with immutable records + git + generated-aggregate verification + milestone snapshots?

options.option: A — keep per-batch full backups (status quo)
options.tradeoffs: Zero policy change and the recovery path every past record describes. Cost: 1.4 MB per batch that grows with the register, 89 near-duplicate files already in the root, and the backup copies the generated aggregate rather than the store, so it no longer protects the thing that is edited.

options.option: B — immutable records + git + milestone snapshots (the plan's proposal)
options.tradeoffs: Recovery becomes git (every record file is committed and never rewritten; validate-split refuses a changed DONE record) plus a tagged snapshot at milestones (e.g. schema-split-baseline-2026-09-08) instead of a copy per batch. Cost: recovery depends on committing at batch close (OPERATORS.md already requires it); an uncommitted working tree has no backup until the record is committed; the standing rule 7 text and every apply script template change.

options.option: C — per-batch backup of the store instead of the aggregate (transitional)
options.tradeoffs: Keeps a backup per batch but of what is actually edited: a zip or a tagged commit of records/, flags/, foundation/ before each batch. Cost: still one artefact per batch; a tag is only useful if committed; a zip is not diffable.

step5_backupPolicy.recommendation: B with a milestone tag at every commit that closes a batch (the finish gate could create it), after the operator confirms; until then A stands.
